title: Military-civil integration key to a robust defence ecosystem to tackle emerging challenges: Raksha Mantri at AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Defence

Military-civil integration key to a robust defence ecosystem to tackle emerging challenges: Raksha Mantri at AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations

“‘Nation First’ a shared commitment of uniformed & civil services; Every element transforms into national strength if the objective is one”
 “AFHQ Civilian Services must evolve into strategic brain of India’s defence management; Research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas vital for strengthening national security”

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
03 AUG 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi

As the Defence Forces are marching towards greater jointness with renewed vigour, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the Ministry of Defence to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security & technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability, and the effective application of rules and regulations. A
ddressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in New Delhi on August 03, 2026,
he emphasised that both the uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.

Raksha Mantri underlined that
military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas - policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences.

“Military officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory. When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,” stated Shri Rajnath Singh.

Explaining with the example of ‘cyber warfare’, Raksha Mantri stated that if officers of the AFHQ Civilian Services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the Defence Forces. He added that a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, the AFHQ Civilian Services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.

Shri Rajnath Singh called upon the AFHQ Civilian Services to evolve into the “strategic brain” of India’s defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.
While he acknowledged the AFHQ Civilian Services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that,
at a time when
modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism,
the cadre
must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.

“A military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must
focus on
strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,” said Raksha Mantri.

As part of the celebrations, Shri Rajnath Singh launched several digital initiatives of the office of Joint Secretary & Chief Administrative Officer (JS & CAO) and its Revised Vision & Mission Statement. The initiatives include Internet-Based Accommodation Management System (IBAMS)
rakshaawas.caomod.gov.in
 portal; Integration of eHRMS with TULIP 2.0 System for processing of claims; Integration of CAO’s Office with TULIP 2.0 for processing of Pay & Allowances; and on-boarding on Smart Performance Appraisal Report Recording Online Window (SPARROW) portal.

Raksha Mantri also released the 34th issue of the ‘Samvad’ magazine that contains travelogues, essays, articles, poems written by employees of various ranks posted in Service Headquarters and Inter-Service Organisations. He also presented awards to AFHQ personnel for their achievements in various fields such as sports, and some of the children of the employees who excelled in academics.

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Additional Secretary Shri Manish Tripathi, JS & CAO Shri Amitabh Prasad and other senior officials were present on the occasion.

AFHQ Day is celebrated on the first day of August every year to recognise the role of the personnel who work shoulder-to-shoulder with Service personnel, primarily in the three Integrated Service Headquarters, Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff and 24 Inter-Service Organisations of the Ministry of Defence. The foundation of AFHQ cadres was laid on August 01, 1942 by organising the then decentralised civilian posts/cadre operation as distinct entities under various Service Headquarters and Secretariat of Ministry of Defence and Finance (Defence) under the control of Chief Administrative Officer.
